title: Kharcha: a 4B model that reads Indian bank SMS so the money stays on your laptop
why_read: A nicely scoped personal project showing a small on-device language model used for genuinely private, practical expense tracking from bank SMS messages.
analysis: Kharcha is a small local app using a 4-billion-parameter open-weight language model to parse Indian bank and UPI SMS messages into structured expense ledger entries, entirely on-device for privacy. It handles multiple Indian banks' SMS formats, payment app notifications, and even casual Hinglish spoken-number input like 'dhai hazaar', and it learns from user corrections over time. The privacy motivation is well-articulated and realistic, since financial SMS data is highly sensitive and most existing finance apps upload it to a server. It's a modest hackathon-style project, but it's a concrete, relatable example of practical small-model on-device NLP rather than another chatbot wrapper.
